books.title: Kaveri: Textbook of English for Grade 9
books.edition: First Edition, January 2026 (Pausha 1947) — new NCERT book for the 2026-27 session; replaces Beehive and Moments

source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's section headings

chapters.title: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read

topics.title: Reading the Story (Part I)
objectives: Student can describe how the narrator read the serial Kashi Yatre aloud to her grandmother, who had never been to school
Student can explain the causes and effects of the grandmother’s tears when the narrator returned from the wedding
visualIdeas: a girl reading a Kannada magazine aloud to her grandmother on a village verandah

topics.title: Reading the Story (Part II)
objectives: Student can describe how the grandmother decided to learn the Kannada alphabet and set Saraswati Puja as her deadline
Student can explain why the narrator says her student ‘passed with flying colours’
visualIdeas: a grandmother tracing letters on a slate while her granddaughter teaches

topics.title: Critical Reflection
objectives: Student can answer extract-based questions on the story with evidence from the text
Student can reflect on the value of literacy and the grandmother’s determination to learn at sixty-two
visualIdeas: an extract card with questions on the grandmother’s feelings

topics.title: Vocabulary and Structures: Binomials, Prefixes, Idioms and the Past Perfect Tense
objectives: Student can use binomials such as ‘hide and seek’ and ‘sooner or later’ in sentences
Student can form opposites with prefixes such as un-, in-, im-, ir-, dis- and mis-
Student can use idioms related to learning, such as ‘burn the midnight oil’
Student can use the past perfect with the simple past to show which of two past actions happened first
visualIdeas: a timeline with two past actions: the earlier in past perfect, the later in simple past

topics.title: Listening and Speaking: Digital Literacy and the Turncoat Debate
objectives: Student can listen to a talk on digital literacy and complete sentences with the exact words heard
Student can argue for and against a topic in a turncoat (solo) debate using suitable phrases
visualIdeas: a speaker switching between ‘for’ and ‘against’ signs

topics.title: Writing Task: Letter to the Editor
objectives: Student can write a formal letter to the editor in the correct format
Student can argue for student participation in adult literacy camps with causes, consequences and suggestions
visualIdeas: a letter-to-the-editor template with sender, date, subject, salutation and body

topics.title: Reading and Appreciating the Poem
objectives: Student can summarise how the poem praises India’s mountains, rivers, scriptures, warriors, sages and music
Student can identify the rhyme scheme, the refrain ‘she’s peerless, let’s praise her!’ and its effect
Student can identify personification, metaphor, symbolism, imagery, hyperbole and allusion, and explain why the poem is an ode
visualIdeas: a map of India with the Himalaya and the Ganga highlighted beside lines from the poem

topics.title: Critical Reflection
objectives: Student can answer extract-based questions on the poem

visualIdeas: an extract from the poem with guiding questions beside it

topics.title: Vocabulary in Context
